## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). I cannot set labels on this repository; suggested: `orig-external`, `cat-enhancements`, `area:sparse_attention`, `op: DSA`, `mod-frost`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

The native DSA training composition (`cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.training`, behind `DSA.sparse_attention`) raised "native sparse attention training currently requires SM100" on every part except cc 10.0. Every native kernel it calls already serves cc 10.3:

- sparse attention forward and backward map cc 10.3 to `sm_103a` (`_ARCH_FLAGS` / `_SM100_FAMILY_ARCH_FLAGS`);
- the top-k compaction and the score recompute gate on SM100+.

The composition now accepts cc 10.0 and 10.3, and `test_DSA_training.py` runs on both.

## Why

On a B300 the composition refused a workload its own kernels serve.

## Related issues

None found.

## API and compatibility impact

None on cc 10.0. On cc 10.3, training through the composition now runs instead of raising `NotImplementedError`.

## Testing

B300 (cc 10.3), develop `64ed3dfe` with its own extension, torch 2.14.1+cu130, cuDNN 9.27.0, CuTe DSL 4.8.1, run from `test/python`:

| Command | develop | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m pytest deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_training.py` | 14 skipped | 14 passed |

Not run on cc 10.0, where the check admits the part exactly as before.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `2f0013d598bb` against base `64ed3dfe1e4d`.

Thank you for your contribution! The new architecture gate preserves the existing training contract, and all 14 focused tests pass on SM100. I found one nonblocking cache issue for a process using both SM100 and SM103 devices.

**[P2] Key the shared compiler and kernel caches by device target** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/2f0013d598bb29f8586675e242b40940ef2f5bc7/python/cudnn/deepseek_sparse_attention/training.py#L51))

Admitting SM103 exposes a mixed-device failure in the training path's dependencies. utils/compiler.py caches gpu_arch_flag() without arguments, so the first GPU's target survives a later device switch. The compaction cache uses only (cols,), and the sparse attention score-recompute cache also omits device/architecture. After training on SM100, training on SM103 can therefore compile or reuse an sm_100a artifact even inside the correct q.device context; the reverse order has the same problem. Please key target selection and these compiled artifacts by the actual device/target, with a regression for both device orders. A host probe confirmed the stale target and same-width artifact reuse; this is a visible mixed-device failure risk, with one architecture per process as a workaround.

Evidence: probe-target-cache.py/log: modeled SM100 then SM103 retained sm_100a for a fresh compile key. Clearing only gpu_arch_flag.cache_clear() selected sm_103a for a fresh key but left the existing width cached as sm_100a. Source inspection confirms the score-recompute key also lacks device/architecture. No foreign-architecture GPU binary was launched. Attribution: The caches predate this PR; widening the training contract newly admits the SM100/SM103 combination that exposes their target mismatch.

Validation: All 14 focused DSA training tests passed on native SM100 using the exact Python head and a compatible native binding. Coverage includes FP32 output/gradient references, sink gradients, score targets, invalid and duplicate sparse metadata, empty rows, length clamps, trusted metadata, NaN suffixes, both checkpoint modes, synchronization guards, and changed-input CUDA Graph replay. A host-only probe confirmed target memoization and compiled compaction artifact reuse across modeled SM100/SM103 contexts. Forward and backward compilation select explicit targets under the input device context; the issue is in the shared compaction and score dependencies. Precheck found no candidates and git diff --check passed. Requested python/misc CI for this head after inspecting the unchanged Style and Security workflows.

Limitations: Native SM103 execution was not independently available. The B300 results in the PR are author-provided evidence; local SM100 tests do not establish SM103 correctness or performance. Pipeline 78124898 is running. Its training-test collection and final outcomes remain unverified. The mixed-device probe models target selection and cache reuse; it does not execute on a physical mixed-GPU system.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

<!-- codex-fe-review:v2:2101:2f0013d598bb29f8586675e242b40940ef2f5bc7:complete:no-blocker -->

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `22bf93a7acd7` against base `f78022abad7b`.

Thank you for your contribution! The follow-up resolves the compiler/cache target P2 from my earlier review. Device capability is read per call; compaction and all changed score-recompute cache keys include the target. The training composition enters the input device context before these calls. No new actionable defect found. The existing approval remains appropriate.

Validation: Exact-head native SM100: 101 unique tests passed across training, sparse score recompute and dense score recompute. The 24 skipped cases require SM90. Coverage includes forward/backward, changed-input graph replay, output/workspace contracts, BF16 and block-scaled dense paths. The two new tests verify compaction and attention-score cache separation with modeled SM100/SM103 targets. An additional compiler-recorder probe checked all four sparse/dense indexer/attention routes in both architecture orders: one compile per target, then reuse of that target's artifact. A bounded host-only helper comparison measured about 0.03 microseconds per call before and 3.46 microseconds after, using nine interleaved rounds. This measures the added device query, not end-to-end GPU performance. Reviewed all five changed files and the training device-context boundaries. Precheck and git diff --check passed. Pipeline 78137243 is running for python/misc; Style and Security workflows were inspected and approved.

Limitations: No independent native SM103 or physical mixed-device run was available. Architecture-switch checks used compiler recorders and launched no foreign-target binary. The author's B300 results remain separate evidence. The first local test invocation omitted a parent fixture: 91 passed, 24 skipped, and 10 setup errors. All ten setup-error cases passed with the correct parent fixture loaded. Both logs are retained. No new GPU timing or determinism guarantee is claimed; kernel arithmetic is unchanged. CI is pending.

Comment only: this PR already has an active approval; preserving existing approvals.

+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+        pytest.skip("native DSA training requires SM100 or SM103")
     from cudnn.frost.buffers import cutedsl_requirement_error
 
     error = cutedsl_requirement_error("DSA training test")
@@ -193,3 +193,41 @@ def step():
         for grad, tensor in zip(actual, (q, kv, a)):
             assert_numerics(grad, tensor.grad, 0.01)
     torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("order", [((10, 0), (10, 3)), ((10, 3), (10, 0))], ids=["sm100_then_sm103", "sm103_then_sm100"])
+def test_compiled_dependencies_follow_the_device_target(monkeypatch, order):
+    """One process may drive an SM100 and an SM103 GPU: the training composition's compiled dependencies (the index compaction and
+    the attention score recompute) take the device's CuTe target per call and key their artifacts by it, so neither part reuses or
+    compiles the other's sm_100a / sm_103a code. Host-modeled: the capability is patched and cute.compile only records its target."""
+    import re
+
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.indexer_top_k import compactify as compact_mod
+    from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.score_recompute import _interface_sm100 as score_mod
+    from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.utils.compiler import _ARCH_MAP, gpu_arch_flag
+
+    compiled = []
+
+    def record(kernel, *args, options=""):
+        compiled.append((type(kernel).__name__, re.search(r"--gpu-arch (\S+)", options).group(1)))
+        return lambda *a, **k: None
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cute, "compile", record)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(compact_mod, "_compile_cache", {})
+    monkeypatch.setattr(score_mod._sparse_attn_score_recompute, "compile_cache", {})
+    idx = torch.tensor([[1, -1, 3, 0], [2, 2, -1, -1]], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    q = torch.zeros(1, 4, 16, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k = torch.zeros(1, 19, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    lse = torch.zeros(1, 4, 16, device="cuda")
+    top = torch.zeros(1, 4, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    out = torch.empty(1, 4, 128, device="cuda")
+    for cc in order + order:
+        monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "get_device_capability", lambda *args, cc=cc: cc)
+        assert gpu_arch_flag() == gpu_arch_flag(idx.device) == _ARCH_MAP[cc]
+        compact_mod.compactify(idx)
+        score_mod.sparse_attn_score_recompute(q, k, lse, top, 512**-0.5, qhead_per_kv_head=16, out=out, topk_indices_global=False)
+    want = [_ARCH_MAP[cc] for cc in order]  # one compile per part; the repeat of each part hits its own artifact
+    assert [arch for name, arch in compiled if name == "CompactifyKernel"] == want, compiled
+    assert [arch for name, arch in compiled if name == "SparseScoreRecomputeSm100"] == want, compiled
+    assert sorted(key[-1] for key in compact_mod._compile_cache) == sorted(want)

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `2f0013d598bb` against base `64ed3dfe1e4d`.

Thank you for your contribution! The new architecture gate preserves the existing training contract, and all 14 focused tests pass on SM100. I found one nonblocking cache issue for a process using both SM100 and SM103 devices.

**[P2] Key the shared compiler and kernel caches by device target** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/2f0013d598bb29f8586675e242b40940ef2f5bc7/python/cudnn/deepseek_sparse_attention/training.py#L51))

Admitting SM103 exposes a mixed-device failure in the training path's dependencies. utils/compiler.py caches gpu_arch_flag() without arguments, so the first GPU's target survives a later device switch. The compaction cache uses only (cols,), and the sparse attention score-recompute cache also omits device/architecture. After training on SM100, training on SM103 can therefore compile or reuse an sm_100a artifact even inside the correct q.device context; the reverse order has the same problem. Please key target selection and these compiled artifacts by the actual device/target, with a regression for both device orders. A host probe confirmed the stale target and same-width artifact reuse; this is a visible mixed-device failure risk, with one architecture per process as a workaround.

Evidence: probe-target-cache.py/log: modeled SM100 then SM103 retained sm_100a for a fresh compile key. Clearing only gpu_arch_flag.cache_clear() selected sm_103a for a fresh key but left the existing width cached as sm_100a. Source inspection confirms the score-recompute key also lacks device/architecture. No foreign-architecture GPU binary was launched. Attribution: The caches predate this PR; widening the training contract newly admits the SM100/SM103 combination that exposes their target mismatch.

Validation: All 14 focused DSA training tests passed on native SM100 using the exact Python head and a compatible native binding. Coverage includes FP32 output/gradient references, sink gradients, score targets, invalid and duplicate sparse metadata, empty rows, length clamps, trusted metadata, NaN suffixes, both checkpoint modes, synchronization guards, and changed-input CUDA Graph replay. A host-only probe confirmed target memoization and compiled compaction artifact reuse across modeled SM100/SM103 contexts. Forward and backward compilation select explicit targets under the input device context; the issue is in the shared compaction and score dependencies. Precheck found no candidates and git diff --check passed. Requested python/misc CI for this head after inspecting the unchanged Style and Security workflows.

Limitations: Native SM103 execution was not independently available. The B300 results in the PR are author-provided evidence; local SM100 tests do not establish SM103 correctness or performance. Pipeline 78124898 is running. Its training-test collection and final outcomes remain unverified. The mixed-device probe models target selection and cache reuse; it does not execute on a physical mixed-GPU system.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
